subject: VPC endpoints, IP allowlist & mTLS integration - next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Mike Chen <mike.chen@finpay.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 15 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: VPC endpoints, IP allowlist & mTLS integration - recap and next steps

Hi Mike —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can keep momentum on the integration: 

Summary from call:
- FinPay will use Redwood Private via VPC Endpoints to keep inference traffic on your network.
- You prefer IP allowlist + egress controls for the initial rollout and plan to evaluate full mTLS for mutual auth.
- Primary use: embeddings + reranker for payment fraud signals; expected volume ~200 req/s initially.
- SDK auth will be token-based (service account key), and you asked about short-lived creds / KMS integration.

Action items (proposed):
1) FinPay: share IP ranges for allowlist + egress path and any firewall rules (attachment: finpay-ip-allowlist.csv).
2) Redwood (Jonas): confirm the VPC endpoint IPs and inbound ports, provide the VPC architecture diagram and suggested routing rules.
3) Redwood (Alex): provide SDK snippet for token-based auth and notes on rotating short-lived tokens (examples for Node/Python).
4) Both teams: decide on mTLS timeline — propose a pilot with mTLS for a subset of routes after IP allowlist is in place.

Attached: draft architecture diagram and mutual-action-plan (MAP) with timeline.

Can you confirm the IP list and whether FinPay needs a static egress IP for outbound callbacks? If so, include the destination IPs/domains.

Thanks —
Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0194

Attachments: redwood-vpc-architecture-diagram.pdf, mutual-action-plan.xlsx

From: Mike Chen <mike.chen@finpay.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Samantha Ortiz <samantha.ortiz@finpay.com>, FinPay SRE Team <sre@finpay.com>
Date: Mon, 17 Aug 2026 10:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: VPC endpoints, IP allowlist & mTLS integration - recap and next steps

Hi Marissa —

Thanks for the clear recap. Confirming below: 

- Attached: finpay-ip-allowlist.csv (internal NAT ranges and our perimeter firewall egress IPs).
- We do need static egress IPs for callbacks to our systems; I'll mark the outbound domains in the CSV.
- mTLS: we'd like to pilot mTLS on the /embed and /rerank routes after the allowlist is live. Our security team prefers mutual auth for production.
- SDK auth: token-based is fine. We currently rotate service account keys every 24 hours via our KMS; can Redwood support short-lived tokens or a token-exchange flow?

Jonas/SRE — can you share the expected client cert requirements (if we go mTLS) and any CA pinning guidance?

Next: we'll review the MAP and aim to have firewall rules updated by Friday.

Cheers,
Mike Chen
Head of Platform Engineering, FinPay
mike.chen@finpay.com

Attachment: finpay-ip-allowlist.csv

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 17 Aug 2026 14:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: VPC endpoints, IP allowlist & mTLS integration - internal owner notes

Marissa / Lauren —

Thanks — looping in technical owners. Notes and proposed owner assignments: 
- I will own the VPC endpoint configuration and provide the subnet-level IPs + ports. Expect a diagram update by EOD tomorrow.
- For mTLS: Redwood can support client certs signed by customer CAs. We recommend exchange of a CSR and pinning the issuing CA in our config. I'll draft the cert requirements (key size, SANs, rotation cadence).
- SDK auth: Alex to provide token-exchange patterns (short-lived tokens issued by Redwood bound to a service account, rotating via KMS).
- Network: we'll need FinPay to confirm if they require outbound SNAT to a single egress IP; if so we'll coordinate NAT gateway config.

I'll prepare a concise checklist for FinPay with the exact firewall rules and sample iptables/ACL entries.

-Jonas
Director, Infrastructure
jonas.weber@redwood.com

From: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.com>
To: Mike Chen <mike.chen@finpay.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 18 Aug 2026 09:38:00 -0700
Subject: Re: VPC endpoints, IP allowlist & mTLS integration - SDK & auth notes

Hi Mike —

Quick follow-up on auth patterns and SDK snippets: 

1) Short-lived tokens: Redwood supports an optional token-exchange flow where FinPay posts a signed assertion (JWT) to our token endpoint and receives a short-lived bearer token (TTL configurable, recommended 15m-1h). We can integrate with your KMS-based rotation; we authorize by verifying signatures against your public key.

2) SDKs: attached are Node and Python examples showing:
- how to perform the token exchange
- how to call embedding + reranker endpoints with streaming and structured output enabled

3) mTLS notes: when you are ready to pilot, we'll provide a CSR template and a sample client cert validation policy. For the pilot, mutual auth can be scoped to specific routes to reduce blast radius.

I'll add the snippets to the MAP in Drive as well.

Best,
Alex Martinez
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
alex.martinez@redwood.com

Attachments: redwood-sdk-examples.zip

From: Mike Chen <mike.chen@finpay.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Cc: Samantha Ortiz <samantha.ortiz@finpay.com>
Date: Tue, 18 Aug 2026 16:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: VPC endpoints, IP allowlist & mTLS integration - next steps

Team —

Appreciate the quick turnaround and clarity. Confirming next steps from our side: 
- Firewall changes scheduled for Thu (will push finpay-ip-allowlist.csv to our perimeter team).
- We want to pilot mTLS on /embed routes after the allowlist goes live; SRE will provision keys and share CSR once we get the template.
- For token exchange: we'll try the short-lived token flow. Please share the public key URL where Redwood will validate assertions.

Marissa — can you send the finalized MAP with target dates and owners once Jonas' checklist is ready? We'll aim for a pilot start the week of Aug 24.

Thanks —
Mike
